# Hannune

> A Seoul-based AI studio building production Graph RAG systems and
AI agents for enterprise teams. Founded 2021. 8+ years of production
AI experience across Netflix, Sony, and LG Energy Solution. 2 AI
optimization patents registered in South Korea.

## What we do

Hannune offers three categories of services:

1. **Graph RAG Consulting** — Productized engagements with fixed
   scope, fixed price, and fixed timeline. Three packages: Starter
   PoC ($8,999, 3 weeks), Standard Production ($38,999, 6 weeks),
   Enterprise Full Agent (custom pricing, 12+ weeks). Plus Ops
   Retainer (from $3,499/month) for ongoing support.

2. **Entity Resolution API** — A SaaS subscription product launching
   Q3 2026. Public tier pricing ($0/$19/$99/$499 per month). Built
   on Splink with LLM disambiguation. Hosted at app.hannune.ai.

3. **2asy.ai** — Graph RAG-powered analytics platform. A separate
   product hosted at 2asy.ai.

## Recent work

- LG Energy Solution: LangGraph-based multi-agent pipeline for
  global talent data acquisition, integrating Crawl4AI and EXAONE.
- Gahyun Tax Accounting: Korean-language tax search system with
  Graph RAG over tax code, precedents, and case files.
- Microsoft Activision CMA Final Report: AI-powered legal and tax
  document search.
- Scenera (TinM AI): Enterprise AI systems for multiple sectors.

## Technical stack

LangGraph, Neo4j, vLLM, FastAPI, Crawl4AI, EXAONE, ElasticSearch,
LiteLLM, Docker. Korean-language NLP and bilingual (Korean/English)
document processing as core specialties.

## Writing

Build-in-public essays on Claude Code, Graph RAG, entity resolution,
and operating autonomous AI agents. Index at https://hannune.ai/blog/

- How I Turned Claude Code Into the Operator of a One-Person AI Company
  (2026-05-26): Moving Claude Code from autocomplete to a production
  operator using a layered CLAUDE.md, seven sub-agents, persistent
  memory, and hard guardrails enforced by hooks. Core thesis: the hard
  part of production AI agents is operational discipline, not prompting.
  https://hannune.ai/blog/claude-code-production-operator.html

- The Real Work in Graph RAG Is Not Extraction (2026-05-26): Building
  the seed knowledge graph for 2asy.ai. Extraction is the easy part.
  The real work is normalization: collapsing 360 relation types into
  80 canonical forms, merging duplicate entities, and fixing evidence
  so the causal graph is walkable. Runs on local GPU hardware.
  https://hannune.ai/blog/graph-rag-normalization.html

- Entity Resolution as an API: How I Built It, Over-Fit It, and Fixed
  It (2026-05-26): Turning entity resolution into a single API call by
  wrapping Splink (open-source, UK Ministry of Justice) with a registry
  that learns aliases over time. Includes an honest account of over-
  fitting a self-built evaluation set and fixing it with a held-out set.
  https://hannune.ai/blog/entity-resolution-api.html

- How I Caught My LLM Fabricating Its Own Evidence (2026-05-30): In the
  2asy.ai knowledge graph the model fabricated the evidence quotes behind
  its own relations, stitching distant sentences together with ellipses.
  Truncating article input made it worse. The fix is a deterministic
  substring check at commit time (the evidence must appear verbatim in the
  source) plus full-body-or-skip collection. Over 500 documents cleaned.
  Core thesis: verify a generator's output with code, not another generator.
  https://hannune.ai/blog/graph-rag-fabricated-evidence.html

- From Vector Search to a Cross-Domain Ontology Graph: How 2asy.ai Reads
  Tariff News (2026-06-03): The retrieval behind 2asy.ai evolved in three
  steps. Plain vector RAG could find similar passages but not represent
  causality. A simple per-article Graph RAG could follow a chain inside one
  document but produced isolated per-document graphs that could not connect
  a cause in one article to its effect in another. The current version runs
  a cross-domain ontology Graph RAG: a shared set of entity, event, and
  relation types plus entity resolution across documents, so the same
  real-world entity becomes one node and causal edges span domains. The
  latest tariff briefing renders its actual causal graph on the page (around
  41 nodes and 60 edges, focused on a Sunset Review root and bridge nodes).
  The graph is thin and partly untyped today; this is a data-accumulation
  problem, not a design ceiling, and it gets denser as more documents flow
  through the same ontology. Runs on local GPU hardware (RTX 4090, W6800).
  https://hannune.ai/blog/cross-domain-ontology-graph-rag.html
